summary: A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Holt studied at Gustavus Adolphus College, the Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He held posts at Bowdoin College (~1978–1988), the University of Calgary (2006), and the University of Chicago.

Nesfield was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Highgate School and Merton College, Oxford. He taught at Highgate School (1859–1864) and held posts at Presidency College, Krishnagar Government College, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (principal, 1878), and the University of Allahabad.

A religious studies scholar, Corrigan earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago. He held appointments at the University of Virginia (~1982–1989), Arizona State University (~1990–2001), and Florida State University as department chair (~2001), among other institutions.

Working in linguistics, history, and archaeology, Crawfurd studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh (~1801–1803). He served as a physician for the East India Company (1803–1808) and succeeded Thomas Stamford Raffles in 1823.

A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, May completed a doctorate in theology at the University of Münster in 1975. He later held academic appointments at Trinity College Dublin, including Associate Professor of Interfaith Dialogue and Professor at the Irish School of Ecumenics.

Dunne works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, having studied at Amherst, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (Ph.D.). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Emory University (~2005–2016), as well as Antioch College and CIHTS.
Kelly is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He has held appointments at the University of Chicago, serving as the Christian W. Mackauer Professor of Anthropology and of Social Sciences.

An Indologist and linguist, Smith served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London (1975). He later joined the University of Cambridge as University Lecturer in Sanskrit (1984) and served as Professor from 2001 to 2007.

A scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, Loori studied at Rutgers and under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Soen Nakagawa. He taught at Naropa University (1974) and served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery from ~1980 to 2009.
Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Buksbazen studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi, Bernie Glassman, and Wendy Egyoku Nakao.

A philosopher who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University, Dewey held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1884–1894), University of Minnesota (~1888–1889), University of Chicago (~1894–1904), and Columbia University (~1904–1930).

An Indologist and linguist who studied under Edwin Norris, Dowson served as a tutor at East India Company College (~1855–1858) and as Professor of Hindustani at both Staff College, Camberley, and University College London (1855–1877).

An Indologist and religious studies scholar, Cort completed a BA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1974) and an AM at Harvard University (~1982–1984). He became a Professor at Denison University starting around 1992.

An Indologist and historian, Richards studied at the University of New Hampshire and the University of California, Berkeley. He held faculty positions at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1977) and Duke University (~1977–2007).

An Indologist and historian educated at Merchant Taylors' School and University College London, Fleet served in the Indian Civil Service and Bombay Civil Service, as Epigraphist to the Government of India (1883–1886), and as Honorary Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society.
Duthie served as Superintendent of the Saharanpur Botanical Garden from ~1876 to 1903 and as Director of the Botanical Survey of India from ~1891 to 1903.

A linguist and Central Asian specialist, Hangin studied at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana University Bloomington. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, and Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1989), also founding The Mongolia Society and the Mongol-American Cultural Association.
A scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology, Griffiths studied at the Royal College of Art. He held an appointment at the Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art from ~1865 to 1895.
Active in Indology, history, and archaeology, Batten was educated at Charterhouse School and the East India Company College (~1827–1829).
An Indologist and historian, Hutton studied at Chigwell School and Worcester College, Oxford (~1903–1908). He served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1909 to 1936.
